questions.q: An excess of $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution is added to $40\text{ mL}$ of a $0.2\text{ M}$ aqueous solution of the complex $\text{PtCl}_4 \cdot 5\text{NH}_3$. Given that the secondary valency of Pt in this complex is 6, the number of moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated is __________ $\times 10^{-3}$.
questions.question: An excess of $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution is added to $40\text{ mL}$ of a $0.2\text{ M}$ aqueous solution of the complex $\text{PtCl}_4 \cdot 5\text{NH}_3$. Given that the secondary valency of Pt in this complex is 6, the number of moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated is __________ $\times 10^{-3}$.
questions.solution:
The secondary valency of Pt is 6, which means its coordination number is 6.

In the complex $\text{PtCl}_4 \cdot 5\text{NH}_3$, to satisfy the secondary valency of 6, five $\text{NH}_3$ molecules and one $\text{Cl}^-$ ion must be present inside the coordination sphere.

The structural formula of the complex is $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_3$.

Upon ionization, one mole of the complex yields three moles of ionizable chloride ions:

$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_3 \rightarrow [\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{3+} + 3\text{Cl}^-$

The number of moles of the complex is given by:

$n = \text{Molarity} \times \text{Volume (in L)} = 0.2 \times 40 \times 10^{-3} = 8 \times 10^{-3} \text{ moles}$

Since each mole of the complex produces 3 moles of $\text{Cl}^-$ ions, the moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated upon adding excess $\text{AgNO}_3$ is:

$3 \times 8 \times 10^{-3} = 24 \times 10^{-3} \text{ moles}$

Answer: $24$

questions.q: The primary and secondary valencies of the central metal ions in $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]$ and $[\text{Pt}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2](\text{NO}_3)_2$ respectively, are:
questions.question: The primary and secondary valencies of the central metal ions in $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]$ and $[\text{Pt}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2](\text{NO}_3)_2$ respectively, are:
questions.solution:
Primary valency corresponds to the oxidation state of the central metal ion.

Secondary valency corresponds to the coordination number of the central metal ion.

For $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]$:
Let the oxidation state of Fe be $x$.
$3(+1) + x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +3$
Primary valency = $3$
Oxalate ($\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$) is a bidentate ligand.
Secondary valency = $3 \times 2 = 6$

For $[\text{Pt}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2](\text{NO}_3)_2$:
Let the oxidation state of Pt be $y$.
$y + 2(0) + 2(-1) + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow y = +4$
Primary valency = $4$
Ethylenediamine (en) is a bidentate ligand and chloride is a monodentate ligand.
Secondary valency = $2 \times 2 + 2 \times 1 = 6$

The primary and secondary valencies are $3, 6$ and $4, 6$ respectively.

Answer: $3, 6$ and $4, 6$

questions.q: An aqueous solution contains $0.024\text{ mol}$ of $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$ and $0.036\text{ mol}$ of $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Cl}$. When an excess of aqueous $\text{BaCl}_2$ is added to this solution, the number of millimoles of precipitate formed is ____.
questions.question: An aqueous solution contains $0.024\text{ mol}$ of $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$ and $0.036\text{ mol}$ of $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Cl}$. When an excess of aqueous $\text{BaCl}_2$ is added to this solution, the number of millimoles of precipitate formed is ____.
questions.solution:
The given coordination compounds ionize in an aqueous solution as follows:

$[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow [\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{2+} + \text{SO}_4^{2-}$

$[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Cl} \rightarrow [\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]^{+} + \text{Cl}^{-}$

When excess aqueous $\text{BaCl}_2$ is added, the $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ ions react only with the free sulfate ions ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$) present in the solution to form a white precipitate of barium sulfate ($\text{BaSO}_4$). The sulfate group in the second complex is inside the coordination sphere and does not ionize.

$\text{Ba}^{2+} + \text{SO}_4^{2-} \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4 \downarrow$

The number of moles of free $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ ions is equal to the number of moles of $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$, which is $0.024\text{ mol}$.

Moles of $\text{BaSO}_4$ precipitate formed $= 0.024\text{ mol}$

To convert this into millimoles:

Millimoles of precipitate $= 0.024 \times 1000 = 24$

Answer: $24$

questions.question: A coordination compound of platinum has the empirical formula $\text{PtCl}_4 \cdot 4\text{NH}_3$. In aqueous solution, its electrical conductivity corresponds to that of a 1:2 electrolyte. The correct coordination formula of the complex is:
questions.solution:
The empirical formula of the given coordination compound is $\text{PtCl}_4 \cdot 4\text{NH}_3$.

The complex behaves as a 1:2 electrolyte in aqueous solution, which means it dissociates to give a total of 3 ions per formula unit (one complex cation and two counter anions).

Analyzing the dissociation of the given options:

$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_4] \cdot 2\text{NH}_3$ does not ionize and acts as a non-electrolyte.

$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4]\text{Cl}_4 \rightarrow [\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{4+} + 4\text{Cl}^{-}$ (1:4 electrolyte, 5 ions).

$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow [\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^{-}$ (1:2 electrolyte, 3 ions).

$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]\text{Cl} \cdot \text{NH}_3 \rightarrow [\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]^{+} + \text{Cl}^{-}$ (1:1 electrolyte, 2 ions).

Thus, the correct coordination formula that corresponds to a 1:2 electrolyte is $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}_2$.

Answer: $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}_2$

questions.q: A $25\text{ mL}$ sample of $0.02\text{ M } [\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_4$ solution is treated with a $0.05\text{ M } \text{AgNO}_3$ solution to completely precipitate the ionisable chloride ions. The minimum volume of the $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution required is:
questions.question: A $25\text{ mL}$ sample of $0.02\text{ M } [\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_4$ solution is treated with a $0.05\text{ M } \text{AgNO}_3$ solution to completely precipitate the ionisable chloride ions. The minimum volume of the $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution required is:
questions.solution:
The number of millimoles of the complex $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_4$ is given by:

$\text{Millimoles} = \text{Molarity} \times \text{Volume in mL} = 0.02 \times 25 = 0.5 \text{ mmol}$

The complex $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_4$ dissociates in solution to give $4$ ionisable $\text{Cl}^-$ ions per formula unit.

$\text{Millimoles of } \text{Cl}^- = 4 \times 0.5 = 2.0 \text{ mmol}$

The precipitation reaction is:

$\text{Ag}^+ + \text{Cl}^- \rightarrow \text{AgCl}(s)$

Since $1$ mole of $\text{Ag}^+$ reacts with $1$ mole of $\text{Cl}^-$, the millimoles of $\text{AgNO}_3$ required is equal to the millimoles of $\text{Cl}^-$.

$\text{Millimoles of } \text{AgNO}_3 = 2.0 \text{ mmol}$

Let $V$ be the volume of $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution required in mL.

$V \times 0.05 = 2.0$

$V = \dfrac{2.0}{0.05} = 40 \text{ mL}$

Answer: $40\text{ mL}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two isomeric coordination complexes $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ have the same empirical formula $\text{CrCl}_3 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Complex $\text{A}$ is violet in colour and its aqueous solution behaves as a $1:3$ electrolyte. Complex $\text{B}$ is grey-green in colour and its aqueous solution behaves as a $1:2$ electrolyte. When $0.01\text{ mol}$ of $\text{A}$ and $0.01\text{ mol}$ of $\text{B}$ are separately dissolved in water and treated with an excess of $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution, what will be the difference in the mass of the precipitate formed in the two cases?
(Given molar mass in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{Ag} = 108$, $\text{Cl} = 35.5$)
questions.question:
Two isomeric coordination complexes $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ have the same empirical formula $\text{CrCl}_3 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Complex $\text{A}$ is violet in colour and its aqueous solution behaves as a $1:3$ electrolyte. Complex $\text{B}$ is grey-green in colour and its aqueous solution behaves as a $1:2$ electrolyte. When $0.01\text{ mol}$ of $\text{A}$ and $0.01\text{ mol}$ of $\text{B}$ are separately dissolved in water and treated with an excess of $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution, what will be the difference in the mass of the precipitate formed in the two cases?
(Given molar mass in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{Ag} = 108$, $\text{Cl} = 35.5$)
questions.solution:
Complex A behaves as a $1:3$ electrolyte, which means it dissociates into one complex cation and three chloride anions. Its formula is $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]\text{Cl}_3$.

Complex B behaves as a $1:2$ electrolyte, which means it dissociates into one complex cation and two chloride anions. Its formula is $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2 \cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

When treated with excess $\text{AgNO}_3$, the ionizable chloride ions precipitate as $\text{AgCl}$.

For $0.01\text{ mol}$ of A, moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated $= 3 \times 0.01 = 0.03\text{ mol}$.

For $0.01\text{ mol}$ of B, moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated $= 2 \times 0.01 = 0.02\text{ mol}$.

Difference in moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitate $= 0.03 - 0.02 = 0.01\text{ mol}$.

Molar mass of $\text{AgCl} = 108 + 35.5 = 143.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

Difference in mass of precipitate $= 0.01 \times 143.5 = 1.435\text{ g}$.

Answer: $1.435\text{ g}$

In the coordination compound $[\text{Cr}(\text{en})_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)]\text{Cl}$ (where $\text{en} = \text{ethane-1,2-diamine}$), let $x$ be the primary valency and $y$ be the secondary valency of the central chromium ion.
The value of $x + y$ is ____.
questions.question:
In the coordination compound $[\text{Cr}(\text{en})_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)]\text{Cl}$ (where $\text{en} = \text{ethane-1,2-diamine}$), let $x$ be the primary valency and $y$ be the secondary valency of the central chromium ion.
The value of $x + y$ is ____.
questions.solution:
The primary valency of a central metal ion in a coordination compound corresponds to its oxidation state.

Let the oxidation state of $\text{Cr}$ be $x$.

In the complex $[\text{Cr}(\text{en})_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)]\text{Cl}$, the ligands are $\text{en}$ (neutral) and $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ (charge $-2$). The counter ion is $\text{Cl}^-$ (charge $-1$).

$x + 2(0) + (-2) + (-1) = 0$

$x = 3$

Thus, the primary valency is $3$.

The secondary valency corresponds to the coordination number of the central metal ion.

Both $\text{en}$ (ethane-1,2-diamine) and $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ (oxalate) are bidentate ligands.

Coordination number $y = 2 \times 2 + 1 \times 2 = 6$

Thus, the secondary valency is $6$.

The value of $x + y = 3 + 6 = 9$.

Answer: $9$

Since there are 6 monodentate $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ligands attached to the central $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ion, the secondary valency is 6.

Answer: $6$

questions.q: An octahedral coordination compound of platinum(IV) has the empirical formula $\text{PtCl}_4 \cdot n(\text{en})$, where $\text{en}$ is ethane-1,2-diamine. When $0.02\text{ mol}$ of this complex is treated with excess aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$, exactly $0.04\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ is precipitated. The value of $n$ is ____.
questions.question: An octahedral coordination compound of platinum(IV) has the empirical formula $\text{PtCl}_4 \cdot n(\text{en})$, where $\text{en}$ is ethane-1,2-diamine. When $0.02\text{ mol}$ of this complex is treated with excess aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$, exactly $0.04\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ is precipitated. The value of $n$ is ____.
questions.solution:
Moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated per mole of the complex = $\dfrac{0.04}{0.02} = 2$

This indicates that there are two ionizable chloride ions present outside the coordination sphere.

(where en = ethane-1,2-diamine)

questions.solution:
Complexes in which the central metal atom or ion is bound to more than one kind of donor group (ligand) are called heteroleptic complexes. Complexes with only one kind of donor group are called homoleptic complexes.

$[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]\text{Cl}_3$ contains only $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ligands $\rightarrow$ Homoleptic.

$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{CO}_3)]\text{Cl}$ contains $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ ligands $\rightarrow$ Heteroleptic.

$\text{K}_3[\text{Al}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]$ contains only $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ ligands $\rightarrow$ Homoleptic.

$[\text{Pt}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^{2+}$ contains en and $\text{Cl}^-$ ligands $\rightarrow$ Heteroleptic.

$[\text{Ni}(\text{en})_3]^{2+}$ contains only en ligands $\rightarrow$ Homoleptic.

$[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$ contains $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{SCN}^-$ ligands $\rightarrow$ Heteroleptic.

The heteroleptic complexes are $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{CO}_3)]\text{Cl}$, $[\text{Pt}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^{2+}$, and $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{SCN})]^{2+}$.

The total number of heteroleptic complexes is $3$.

questions.solution:
Mohr's salt is a double salt with the formula $\text{FeSO}_4 \cdot (\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$. In aqueous solution, it completely dissociates into simple ions ($\text{Fe}^{2+}$, $\text{NH}_4^+$, and $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$). Thus, statement (A) is correct.

Potash alum ($\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 \cdot \text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 \cdot 24\text{H}_2\text{O}$) is a double salt, not a coordination compound. Thus, statement (B) is incorrect.

$\text{K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$ is a coordination compound. In aqueous solution, it dissociates into $4\text{K}^+$ and the complex ion $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$. The complex ion does not further dissociate into $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\text{CN}^-$ ions. Thus, statement (C) is correct.

Carnallite ($\text{KCl} \cdot \text{MgCl}_2 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$) is a double salt. Thus, statement (D) is correct.

Therefore, statements (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

Answer: (A), (C) and (D) only

$\text{AlCl}_3$: Aluminum is electron-deficient and acts as a Lewis acid. It cannot act as a ligand.

The species that can act as ligands are $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{CO}$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, and $\text{NCS}^-$.

The total number of such species is $4$.

questions.question: Consider the coordination compound $[\text{Pt}(\text{en})(\text{NH}_3)_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)]\text{SO}_4$, where (en) is ethane-1,2-diamine. Let $x$ be the coordination number and $y$ be the oxidation state of the central platinum ion. The value of $x + y$ is:
questions.solution:
The given coordination compound is $[\text{Pt}(\text{en})(\text{NH}_3)_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)]\text{SO}_4$.

The ligands present in the coordination sphere are:
Ethane-1,2-diamine (en): a neutral bidentate ligand.
Ammine ($\text{NH}_3$): a neutral monodentate ligand.
Oxalato ($\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$): a dinegative bidentate ligand.

The coordination number $x$ is the total number of ligand donor atoms bonded to the central metal ion.

$x = 1 \times 2 \text{ (from en)} + 2 \times 1 \text{ (from NH}_3) + 1 \times 2 \text{ (from C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}) = 6$

The oxidation state $y$ of Pt is calculated by equating the sum of oxidation states to the charge of the complex ion $[\text{Pt}(\text{en})(\text{NH}_3)_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)]^{2+}$.

$y + 0 + 2(0) + (-2) = +2$

$y = 4$

The value of $x + y = 6 + 4 = 10$.

Answer: 10

questions.solution:
An ambidentate ligand is a monodentate ligand that contains more than one coordinating atom but binds to the central metal ion through only one donor atom at a time.

In the thiocyanate ion ($\text{SCN}^-$), there are two possible donor atoms: sulfur (S) and nitrogen (N). It can coordinate to the metal center either through the sulfur atom (forming thiocyanato complexes) or through the nitrogen atom (forming isothiocyanato complexes).

Acetate ion and azide ion coordinate through only one type of atom (oxygen and nitrogen, respectively). Glycinate ion is a bidentate ligand that coordinates simultaneously through nitrogen and oxygen.

Therefore, the thiocyanate ion is an ambidentate ligand.

Answer: Thiocyanate ion ($\text{SCN}^-$)

questions.question: An octahedral coordination entity is formed by a central $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ion surrounded by two oxalate ions, one hydroxide ion and one aqua molecule. The net charge on this complex is $-x$. The value of $x$ is ____.
questions.solution:
The central metal ion is $\text{Cr}^{3+}$, which has a charge of $+3$.

The ligands present in the coordination entity are:
Two oxalate ions ($\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$), each with a charge of $-2$.
One hydroxide ion ($\text{OH}^{-}$), with a charge of $-1$.
One aqua molecule ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$), which is neutral and has a charge of $0$.

The net charge on the complex is the sum of the charges of the central metal ion and all the ligands.

Net charge $= +3 + 2(-2) + 1(-1) + 1(0)$

Net charge $= +3 - 4 - 1 + 0 = -2$

The net charge is given as $-x$.

$-x = -2 \Rightarrow x = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.q: When one mole of the coordination compound formulated as $\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4\text{NH}_3$ is treated with excess aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution, exactly one mole of $\text{AgCl}$ is precipitated. The coordination number of the central cobalt ion in this complex is:
questions.question: When one mole of the coordination compound formulated as $\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4\text{NH}_3$ is treated with excess aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution, exactly one mole of $\text{AgCl}$ is precipitated. The coordination number of the central cobalt ion in this complex is:
questions.solution:
The precipitation of exactly one mole of $\text{AgCl}$ per mole of the complex indicates that there is only one ionizable chloride ion present outside the coordination sphere.

The remaining two chloride ions and the four ammonia molecules must be present inside the coordination sphere, bonded directly to the central cobalt ion.

The structural formula of the complex is $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}$.

The number of ligands directly attached to the central metal ion is $4 + 2 = 6$.

Thus, the coordination number of the central cobalt ion is $6$.

Answer: $6$

questions.solution:
The coordination number is the total number of ligand donor atoms to which the metal is directly bonded.

For $[\text{Ni}(\text{en})_3]\text{Cl}_2$, ethylenediamine (en) is a bidentate ligand. Since there are $3$ en ligands, the coordination number $x = 3 \times 2 = 6$.

For $[\text{Zn}(\text{EDTA})]^{2-}$, ethylenediaminetetraacetate (EDTA) is a hexadentate ligand. Since there is $1$ EDTA ligand, the coordination number $y = 1 \times 6 = 6$.

For $[\text{Pd}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_2]^{2-}$, oxalate ($\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$) is a bidentate ligand. Since there are $2$ oxalate ligands, the coordination number $z = 2 \times 2 = 4$.

Thus, $x = 6$, $y = 6$, and $z = 4$.

Answer: $x=6, y=6, z=4$

$\text{Na}_3[\text{Co}(\text{NO}_2)_6]$

The number of compounds in which a complex ion is named first in their IUPAC nomenclature is ____.
questions.solution:
In the IUPAC nomenclature of coordination compounds, the cation is always named before the anion. Therefore, a complex ion is named first only if it acts as the cation in the given compound.

Let us analyze the given compounds:
$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$: The cation is the complex ion $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$. It is named first.
$\text{K}_3[\text{Al}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]$: The cation is the simple ion $\text{K}^+$. It is named first.
$[\text{Pt}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]\text{SO}_4$: The cation is the complex ion $[\text{Pt}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^{2+}$. It is named first.
$\text{K}_2[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]$: The cation is the simple ion $\text{K}^+$. It is named first.
$[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2][\text{Ag}(\text{CN})_2]$: The cation is the complex ion $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+$. It is named first.
$\text{Na}_3[\text{Co}(\text{NO}_2)_6]$: The cation is the simple ion $\text{Na}^+$. It is named first.

Thus, there are $3$ compounds in which a complex ion is named first.

Answer: $3$

questions.question: The correct IUPAC name of the complex $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_3(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$ is:
questions.solution:
The given complex is $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$.

The ligands present in the coordination sphere are:
$\text{NH}_3$ $\rightarrow$ ammine (3 ligands $\rightarrow$ triammine)
$\text{H}_2\text{O}$ $\rightarrow$ aqua (2 ligands $\rightarrow$ diaqua)
$\text{Cl}^-$ $\rightarrow$ chlorido (1 ligand $\rightarrow$ chlorido)

According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, ligands are named in alphabetical order, ignoring the numerical prefixes. The alphabetical order is ammine, aqua, chlorido.

Let the oxidation state of Cobalt be $x$. The complex ion is $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2\text{Cl}]^{2+}$ because there are two chloride ions outside the coordination sphere.
$x + 3(0) + 2(0) + 1(-1) = +2$
$x = +3$

The central metal is named cobalt since the complex ion is a cation, followed by its oxidation state in Roman numerals in parentheses: cobalt(III).

The anion outside the coordination sphere is chloride.

Combining these parts, the correct IUPAC name is Triamminediaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride.

Answer: Triamminediaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride

questions.question: The correct IUPAC name of the coordination compound $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_2\text{(H}_2\text{O)}_2\text{(en)}]\text{Cl}_3$ is:
questions.solution:
The complex ion is $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_2\text{(H}_2\text{O)}_2\text{(en)}]^{3+}$ and the counter ion is $\text{Cl}^-$.

The ligands present in the coordination sphere are:
$\text{NH}_3$ $\rightarrow$ ammine
$\text{H}_2\text{O}$ $\rightarrow$ aqua
$\text{en}$ $\rightarrow$ ethane-1,2-diamine

According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, ligands are named in alphabetical order. Comparing 'ammine' and 'aqua', 'ammine' comes first since 'm' precedes 'q'. Thus, the order is ammine, aqua, and then ethane-1,2-diamine.

Since there are two $\text{NH}_3$ and two $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ molecules, the prefixes 'di' are used, resulting in 'diammine' and 'diaqua'. Note that 'ammine' is spelled with a double 'm'.

Let the oxidation state of cobalt be $x$.
$x + 2(0) + 2(0) + 1(0) = +3$
$x = +3$

The central metal is named cobalt(III) because the complex is cationic.

The counter ion is named simply as chloride, without any numerical prefix for the number of ions.

Combining these parts, the correct IUPAC name is Diamminediaqua(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) chloride.

Answer: Diamminediaqua(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) chloride

questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The IUPAC name of the ligand $\text{SCN}^-$ when it coordinates to a central metal through the sulphur atom is thiocyanato-N.
Statement II: In the IUPAC nomenclature of coordination compounds, the names of anionic ligands ending in '-ate' are modified to end in '-ito'.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution:
Statement I is incorrect because the ambidentate ligand $\text{SCN}^{-}$ coordinating to a central metal through the sulphur atom is named thiocyanato-S, whereas when it coordinates through the nitrogen atom, it is named thiocyanato-N.

Statement II is incorrect because in the IUPAC nomenclature of coordination compounds, the names of anionic ligands ending in '-ate' are modified to end in '-ato' (for example, sulphate becomes sulphato). The suffix '-ito' is used for anionic ligands ending in '-ite' (for example, nitrite becomes nitrito).

Therefore, both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

The complex consists of the cationic coordination sphere $[\text{Co(en)}_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)]^+$ and the counter anion $\text{Cl}^-$.

The oxidation state of cobalt, $x$, is calculated as:

$x + 2(0) + (-2) = +1 \Rightarrow x = +3$

The ligands are named in alphabetical order. The ligand 'en' is ethane-1,2-diamine and $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ is oxalato. Since 'e' comes before 'o', ethane-1,2-diamine is written first.

Because the name of the bidentate ligand ethane-1,2-diamine contains numbers, the prefix 'bis' is used to indicate two such ligands.

As the complex ion is a cation, the central metal is named cobalt followed by its oxidation state in Roman numerals.

Combining these rules, the correct IUPAC name is Bis(ethane-1,2-diamine)oxalatocobalt(III) chloride.

Answer: Bis(ethane-1,2-diamine)oxalatocobalt(III) chloride

In the coordination compound $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2(\text{NH}_3)\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$ (where en = ethane-1,2-diamine), the coordination number and the oxidation state of the central cobalt atom are $x$ and $y$, respectively.
The value of $x + y$ is ____.
questions.question:
In the coordination compound $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2(\text{NH}_3)\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$ (where en = ethane-1,2-diamine), the coordination number and the oxidation state of the central cobalt atom are $x$ and $y$, respectively.
The value of $x + y$ is ____.
questions.solution:
The coordination number $x$ is the total number of ligand donor atoms bonded to the central metal ion.

In $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2(\text{NH}_3)\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$, the ligands are:
Two ethane-1,2-diamine (en) molecules, which are bidentate ligands, contributing $2 \times 2 = 4$ donor atoms.
One ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) molecule, which is a monodentate ligand, contributing $1$ donor atom.
One chloride ($\text{Cl}^{-}$) ion, which is a monodentate ligand, contributing $1$ donor atom.

Coordination number $x = 4 + 1 + 1 = 6$.

To find the oxidation state $y$ of cobalt, we set up the charge balance equation. The sulfate counterion ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$) has a charge of $-2$, so the complex ion is $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2(\text{NH}_3)\text{Cl}]^{2+}$.

$y + 2(0) + 1(0) + 1(-1) = +2$

$y - 1 = 2 \Rightarrow y = 3$

The value of $x + y = 6 + 3 = 9$.

Answer: $9$

questions.question:

Statement I: The chemical formula for the coordination compound iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II) is $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]_3$.
Statement II: The chemical formula for the coordination compound potassium tetracyanidonickelate(II) is $\text{K}_2[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]$.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution:
In Statement I, the oxidation state of iron outside the coordination sphere is $+3$, which corresponds to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$. The complex ion is hexacyanidoferrate(II), which means iron inside the coordination sphere is in the $+2$ oxidation state. Since there are six cyanide ligands (each with a $-1$ charge), the charge on the complex ion is $+2 + 6(-1) = -4$, giving $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$. To balance the charges, four $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions will combine with three $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$ ions, resulting in the formula $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]_3$. Thus, Statement I is correct.

In Statement II, the cation is potassium, $\text{K}^+$. The complex ion is tetracyanidonickelate(II), which means nickel is in the $+2$ oxidation state. With four cyanide ligands, the charge on the complex ion is $+2 + 4(-1) = -2$, giving $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$. To balance the charges, two $\text{K}^+$ ions are required for one complex ion, resulting in the formula $\text{K}_2[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]$. Thus, Statement II is also correct.

Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

questions.question: The total number of ionisation isomers possible for the coordination compound $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2(\text{Br})\text{Cl}]\text{NO}_3$ (including the given compound) is ____.
questions.solution:
The given coordination compound is $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2(\text{Br})\text{Cl}]\text{NO}_3$.

Ionisation isomerism arises when a ligand from the coordination sphere exchanges places with a counter ion outside the coordination sphere, producing different ions in aqueous solution.

In the given complex, the anionic ligands available for exchange are $\text{Br}^-$, $\text{Cl}^-$, and $\text{NO}_3^-$. By exchanging the positions of these monoanionic groups between the inner coordination sphere and the outer sphere, we get the following possible ionisation isomers:

1. $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2(\text{Br})\text{Cl}]\text{NO}_3$ (furnishes $\text{NO}_3^-$ ion in solution)
2. $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2(\text{Br})(\text{NO}_3)]\text{Cl}$ (furnishes $\text{Cl}^-$ ion in solution)
3. $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2(\text{Cl})(\text{NO}_3)]\text{Br}$ (furnishes $\text{Br}^-$ ion in solution)

Thus, there are exactly 3 ionisation isomers possible for the given molecular formula.

Answer: $3$

(B) $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]\text{NO}_2$ and $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2(\text{NO}_2)\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}$ are an example of ionisation isomers.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct. The complex $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4$ yields $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ ions in aqueous solution, which react with $\text{BaCl}_2$ to form a white precipitate of $\text{BaSO}_4$. The complex $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{SO}_4)]\text{Br}$ yields $\text{Br}^-$ ions in solution, which do not form a precipitate with $\text{BaCl}_2$. Thus, they can be chemically distinguished.

Statement (C) is incorrect. Ionisation isomerism arises when a counter ion in a complex salt is itself a potential ligand and can displace a ligand, which can then become the counter ion. questions.question: Which of the following pairs of coordination compounds exhibits coordination isomerism?

Coordination isomerism occurs in compounds containing both complex cations and complex anions. It arises from the interchange of ligands between the cationic and anionic entities of the different metal ions present in the complex.

The pair $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Br}_2$ and $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Br}_2]\text{Cl}_2$ exhibits ionization isomerism.

$[\text{Cr(NH}_3)_4(\text{NO}_2)_2]^+$, $[\text{Mn(H}_2\text{O})_4\text{Cl}_2]$, $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]^{2+}$, $[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^{2+}$, $[\text{Ni(NH}_3)_6]^{2+}$, $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O})_4(\text{SCN})_2]^+$
questions.solution:
Geometrical isomerism in octahedral complexes is typically exhibited by complexes of the type $MA_4B_2$, $MA_3B_3$, $M(AA)_2B_2$, etc., where $A$ and $B$ are monodentate ligands and $AA$ is a bidentate ligand.

Let us analyze the given complexes:

1. $[\text{Cr(NH}_3)_4(\text{NO}_2)_2]^+$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_4B_2$. It can exist in cis and trans forms.

2. $[\text{Mn(H}_2\text{O})_4\text{Cl}_2]$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_4B_2$. It can exist in cis and trans forms.

3. $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]^{2+}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_5B$. It does not exhibit geometrical isomerism because all positions relative to the single $B$ ligand are equivalent.

4. $[\text{Pt(NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^{2+}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_4B_2$. It can exist in cis and trans forms.

5. $[\text{Ni(NH}_3)_6]^{2+}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_6$. It does not exhibit geometrical isomerism.

6. $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O})_4(\text{SCN})_2]^+$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_4B_2$. It can exist in cis and trans forms.

Thus, there are $4$ complexes that can exhibit cis-trans geometrical isomerism.

Answer: $4$

questions.question:

The number of $\text{Cl}-\text{Cr}-\text{Cl}$ bond angle(s) of $90^\circ$ present in this isomer is ____.
questions.solution:
The given complex $[\text{Cr(NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]$ is of the type $MA_3B_3$.

It exhibits facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomerism.

In the meridional (mer) isomer, the three identical ligands ($\text{Cl}^-$) are arranged around the meridian of the octahedron. Two of the $\text{Cl}^-$ ligands are trans to each other (at an angle of $180^\circ$), while the third $\text{Cl}^-$ ligand is cis to both of them.

Thus, the $\text{Cl}-\text{Cr}-\text{Cl}$ bond angles in the mer isomer are one $180^\circ$ angle and two $90^\circ$ angles.

Therefore, the number of $\text{Cl}-\text{Cr}-\text{Cl}$ bond angles of $90^\circ$ is $2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.solution:

Such octahedral complexes exhibit geometrical isomerism, specifically facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomers, depending on whether three identical ligands occupy the corners of an octahedral face or a meridian.

Reason (R) is true because the central chromium atom is in the $+3$ oxidation state with a $3d^3$ electronic configuration. The three electrons singly occupy the $t_{2g}$ orbitals, leaving two $e_g$ orbitals empty. These two inner $3d$ orbitals, along with one $4s$ and three $4p$ orbitals, undergo $d^2sp^3$ hybridization, resulting in an octahedral geometry.

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A). The existence of fac and mer isomers is specifically due to the $MA_3B_3$ composition and the different possible spatial arrangements of the ligands, not merely because the complex has an octahedral geometry (as many octahedral complexes do not show this isomerism).

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

Since the bidentate ligand (en) can only span adjacent (cis) positions, there is only one possible spatial arrangement for the ligands. Hence, it does not show geometrical isomerism. Thus, statement (D) is correct.

Therefore, only statements (A) and (D) are correct.

The value of $x + y + z$ is ____.
questions.solution:
The given complex ion is $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$.

Let the oxidation state of cobalt be $x$.
$x + 6(-1) = -3 \Rightarrow x = +3$
Thus, $x = 3$.

The coordination number of cobalt in $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$ is $6$. According to Valence Bond Theory, the central metal ion provides a number of vacant hybrid orbitals equal to its coordination number to accept electron pairs from the ligands. Therefore, the number of vacant hybrid orbitals is $6$.
Thus, $y = 6$.

The atomic number of Co is $27$. Its electronic configuration is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7 4s^2$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$.
Since $\text{F}^-$ is a weak field ligand, it does not cause the pairing of electrons in the $3d$ orbitals against Hund's rule. The complex forms an outer orbital complex with $sp^3d^2$ hybridization.
The $6$ electrons in the $3d$ subshell are arranged as one pair and four unpaired electrons.
Thus, the number of unpaired electrons is $z = 4$.

The value of $x + y + z = 3 + 6 + 4 = 13$.

Answer: $13$

questions.question:
The hybridisation and the spin-only magnetic moment of the complex $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$, respectively, are:
(Given: atomic number of $\text{Mn} = 25$)
questions.solution:
The oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ in $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ is $+3$.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}$ (atomic number $25$) is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4$.

Since $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of electrons. In an octahedral field, the $3d^4$ electrons will occupy the lower energy $t_{2g}$ orbitals, giving the configuration $t_{2g}^4 e_g^0$.

The number of unpaired electrons is $n = 2$.

The spin-only magnetic moment is given by $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$.

Substituting $n = 2$, we get $\mu = \sqrt{2(2+2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83 \text{ BM}$.

Since the two $e_g$ orbitals of the $3d$ subshell are empty, they participate in hybridisation along with one $4s$ and three $4p$ orbitals.

Therefore, the hybridisation of the complex is $d^2sp^3$.

Answer: $d^2sp^3$ and $2.83 \text{ BM}$

In $[\text{Cu(CN)}_4]^{3-}$, $\text{Cu}^{+}$ is a $3d^{10}$ system. It undergoes $sp^3$ hybridization, forming a tetrahedral, diamagnetic complex.

questions.solution:
The spin-only magnetic moment is given by $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{ BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given $\mu \approx 4.90\text{ BM}$, we have $\sqrt{n(n+2)} = 4.90$, which gives $n = 4$.

The oxidation state of $\text{Co}$ is $+2$. The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7$. Since $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is a weak field ligand, the configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^2$. The number of unpaired electrons is $n = 3$.

The oxidation state of $\text{V}$ is $+3$. The electronic configuration of $\text{V}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^2$. The number of unpaired electrons is $n = 2$. It forms an inner-orbital complex ($d^2sp^3$).

Thus, $[\text{MnF}_6]^{3-}$ is the outer-orbital complex with $4$ unpaired electrons and a magnetic moment of approximately $4.90\text{ BM}$.

questions.question: The hybridisation of the central metal ion in the complexes $[\text{Zn(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ and $[\text{Pd(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$, respectively, is:
questions.solution:
For $[\text{Zn(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$:
The central metal ion is $\text{Zn}^{2+}$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10}$.
Since the $3d$ subshell is completely filled, no inner $d$-orbital is available for hybridization.
The complex uses one $4s$ and three $4p$ orbitals to accommodate the electron pairs from the four $\text{NH}_3$ ligands.
Thus, the hybridization is $sp^3$ and the geometry is tetrahedral.

For $[\text{Pd(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$:
The central metal ion is $\text{Pd}^{2+}$.
The electronic configuration of $\text{Pd}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Kr}] 4d^8$.
Since Pd belongs to the $4d$ transition series, the crystal field splitting energy is large, and all ligands effectively behave as strong field ligands.
The eight $4d$ electrons pair up in four $d$-orbitals, leaving one $4d$ orbital empty.
The complex uses one $4d$, one $5s$, and two $5p$ orbitals for hybridization.
Thus, the hybridization is $dsp^2$ and the geometry is square planar.

The hybridizations are $sp^3$ and $dsp^2$, respectively.

Answer: $sp^3$ and $dsp^2$

5. It does not make exact predictions regarding the tetrahedral and square planar structures of 4-coordinate complexes without prior knowledge of magnetic data.
6. It does not distinguish between weak and strong ligands.

If the specific orbital hybridisation of a complex is already known (for example, $sp^3$ or $dsp^2$), VBT can accurately predict its exact geometry (tetrahedral or square planar, respectively). Therefore, the statement that it cannot predict the exact geometry if the hybridisation is known is incorrect, making it not a limitation of VBT.

Answer: It cannot predict the exact geometry of a complex if the specific orbital hybridisation is already known.

questions.question: During the formation of an octahedral coordination complex, the five $d$-orbitals of the central metal ion split into two sets due to the electrostatic field of the approaching ligands. The set of orbitals that experiences the minimum electrostatic repulsion from the ligands, and is consequently stabilized relative to the barycentre, consists of:
questions.solution:
In an octahedral coordination complex, the ligands approach the central metal ion along the coordinate axes ($x$, $y$, and $z$ axes).

The $d$-orbitals that point directly along these axes are $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{z^2}$ (the $e_g$ set). These orbitals experience maximum electrostatic repulsion from the approaching ligands and are destabilized relative to the barycentre.

The $d$-orbitals that point between the axes are $d_{xy}$, $d_{yz}$, and $d_{zx}$ (the $t_{2g}$ set). These orbitals experience minimum electrostatic repulsion from the ligands and are consequently stabilized relative to the barycentre.

Thus, the stabilized set consists of $d_{xy}$, $d_{yz}$, and $d_{zx}$.

Answer: $d_{xy}$, $d_{yz}$ and $d_{zx}$

questions.q: In an octahedral coordination entity, the five d-orbitals of the central metal ion split into two sets. The energy of the $e_g$ set is raised by $x\Delta_\text{o}$ and that of the $t_{2g}$ set is lowered by $y\Delta_\text{o}$ with respect to the hypothetical spherical crystal field. The values of $x$ and $y$ are respectively:
questions.question: In an octahedral coordination entity, the five d-orbitals of the central metal ion split into two sets. The energy of the $e_g$ set is raised by $x\Delta_\text{o}$ and that of the $t_{2g}$ set is lowered by $y\Delta_\text{o}$ with respect to the hypothetical spherical crystal field. The values of $x$ and $y$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
In an octahedral crystal field, the five degenerate d-orbitals split into two sets: a doubly degenerate $e_g$ set and a triply degenerate $t_{2g}$ set.

The total crystal field splitting energy is denoted by $\Delta_\text{o}$.

To maintain the barycenter (center of gravity) of the energy levels, the total energy change must be zero. If the energy of the $e_g$ set is raised by $x\Delta_\text{o}$ and the $t_{2g}$ set is lowered by $y\Delta_\text{o}$, we have:

$2x - 3y = 0$

Also, the total energy difference between the two sets is $\Delta_\text{o}$, which gives:

$x + y = 1$

Solving these two equations:

$2(1 - y) - 3y = 0$

$2 - 5y = 0 \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{2}{5} = 0.4$

$x = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$

Thus, the energy of the $e_g$ set is raised by $0.6\Delta_\text{o}$ and that of the $t_{2g}$ set is lowered by $0.4\Delta_\text{o}$.

questions.explanation:
In an octahedral crystal field, the five degenerate d-orbitals split into two sets: a doubly degenerate $e_g$ set and a triply degenerate $t_{2g}$ set.

The total crystal field splitting energy is denoted by $\Delta_\text{o}$.

To maintain the barycenter (center of gravity) of the energy levels, the total energy change must be zero. If the energy of the $e_g$ set is raised by $x\Delta_\text{o}$ and the $t_{2g}$ set is lowered by $y\Delta_\text{o}$, we have:

$2x - 3y = 0$

Also, the total energy difference between the two sets is $\Delta_\text{o}$, which gives:

$x + y = 1$

Solving these two equations:

$2(1 - y) - 3y = 0$

$2 - 5y = 0 \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{2}{5} = 0.4$

$x = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$

Thus, the energy of the $e_g$ set is raised by $0.6\Delta_\text{o}$ and that of the $t_{2g}$ set is lowered by $0.4\Delta_\text{o}$.

Answer: $0.6$ and $0.4$

The crystal field stabilisation energy (CFSE) is given by:

$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times n_{t_{2g}} + 0.6 \times n_{e_g}) \Delta_o$

Substituting the number of electrons:

$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times 3 + 0.6 \times 1) \Delta_o = -0.6 \Delta_o$

Answer: $-0.6 \Delta_\text{o}$

The total increase in energy of the $e_g$ set is $2 \times 0.6 \Delta_o = 1.2 \Delta_o$.

Since the total decrease in energy is numerically equal to the total increase in energy, Statement I is incorrect.

The barycentre is defined as the average energy of the five $d$-orbitals in a hypothetical spherical crystal field. Thus, Statement II is correct.

Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

The spin-only magnetic moment is given by $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

For $n = 2$ unpaired electrons, the possible configurations are $d^2$ and $d^8$.

For a $d^2$ configuration, the arrangement is $t_{2g}^2 e_g^0$.
$\text{CFSE} = 2 \times (-0.4\Delta_\text{o}) = -0.8\Delta_\text{o}$.

For a $d^8$ configuration, the arrangement is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^2$.
$\text{CFSE} = 6 \times (-0.4\Delta_\text{o}) + 2 \times (0.6\Delta_\text{o}) = -2.4\Delta_\text{o} + 1.2\Delta_\text{o} = -1.2\Delta_\text{o}$.

The neutral metal $\text{M}$ has the configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8 4s^2$.

For $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$, $\text{Cr}$ is in $+3$ oxidation state with a $d^3$ configuration. The electronic arrangement in an octahedral field is $t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$.

When this ion is placed in a tetrahedral crystal field, the number of d-orbitals from the given list that are raised in energy relative to the barycentre is ____.
questions.solution:
In a tetrahedral crystal field, the approaching ligands are directed between the Cartesian axes.

The d-orbitals whose lobes lie between the axes ($d_{xy}$, $d_{yz}$, $d_{zx}$) experience greater electrostatic repulsion from the ligands. These three orbitals form the $t_2$ set and are raised in energy by $0.4 \Delta_t$ relative to the barycentre.

The d-orbitals whose lobes lie along the axes ($d_{x^2-y^2}$, $d_{z^2}$) experience less repulsion. These two orbitals form the $e$ set and are lowered in energy by $0.6 \Delta_t$ relative to the barycentre.

Therefore, the number of d-orbitals raised in energy is $3$.

Answer: $3$

questions.solution:
In a tetrahedral crystal field, the ligands approach the central metal ion between the coordinate axes.

The d-orbitals lying between the axes ($d_{xy}$, $d_{yz}$, $d_{zx}$) experience greater repulsion from the ligands and are raised in energy, forming the higher energy $t_2$ set.

The d-orbitals lying along the axes ($d_{x^2-y^2}$, $d_{z^2}$) experience lesser repulsion and are lowered in energy relative to the barycentre, forming the lower energy $e$ set.

This splitting pattern is exactly inverted compared to an octahedral crystal field, where the $e_g$ set is higher in energy and the $t_{2g}$ set is lower in energy.

The tetrahedral crystal field splitting energy is given by $\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9} \Delta_o$, which means it is smaller than the octahedral splitting energy for the same metal and ligands.

Therefore, the statement regarding the inverted splitting pattern is the only correct one.

The predicted tetrahedral splitting energy ($\Delta_\text{t}$) for the hypothetical complex $[\text{Ni(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ (assuming identical metal-ligand bond lengths) is:
questions.solution:
The relationship between the crystal field splitting energy in a tetrahedral field ($\Delta_t$) and an octahedral field ($\Delta_o$) for the same metal, ligands, and metal-ligand bond lengths is given by:

Substituting the given value:

$\Delta_t = \dfrac{4}{9} \times 10800 \text{ cm}^{-1}$

$\Delta_t = 4 \times 1200 \text{ cm}^{-1} = 4800 \text{ cm}^{-1}$

Answer: $4800 \text{ cm}^{-1}$

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding tetrahedral coordination complexes:
(A) In $[\text{MnBr}_4]^{2-}$, the $e$ set of orbitals contains exactly 2 electrons.
(B) In $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, the $t_2$ set of orbitals contains exactly 4 electrons.
(C) In $[\text{CoBr}_4]^{2-}$, the $t_2$ set of orbitals contains exactly 3 electrons.
(D) In $[\text{Zn(OH)}_4]^{2-}$, the $e$ set contains more electrons than the $t_2$ set.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In tetrahedral complexes, the $d$-orbitals split into a lower energy $e$ set (doubly degenerate) and a higher energy $t_2$ set (triply degenerate). Due to the small crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_t$), tetrahedral complexes are generally high-spin.

For $[\text{MnBr}_4]^{2-}$, Mn is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^5$). The electronic configuration is $e^2 t_2^3$. The $e$ set contains exactly 2 electrons. Statement (A) is correct.

For $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, Ni is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^8$). The electronic configuration is $e^4 t_2^4$. The $t_2$ set contains exactly 4 electrons. Statement (B) is correct.

For $[\text{CoBr}_4]^{2-}$, Co is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^7$). The electronic configuration is $e^4 t_2^3$. The $t_2$ set contains exactly 3 electrons. Statement (C) is correct.

For $[\text{Zn(OH)}_4]^{2-}$, Zn is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^{10}$). The electronic configuration is $e^4 t_2^6$. The $e$ set contains 4 electrons and the $t_2$ set contains 6 electrons. Thus, the $e$ set contains fewer electrons than the $t_2$ set. Statement (D) is incorrect.

Therefore, statements (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

Answer: (A), (B) and (C) only

Match List-I (Tetrahedral complexes) with List-II (Magnitude of Crystal Field Stabilization Energy, CFSE, ignoring pairing energy).
List-IList-II
(A)$[\text{ZnCl}_4]^{2-}$(I)$0.0\,\Delta_t$
(B)$[\text{CuCl}_4]^{2-}$(II)$0.4\,\Delta_t$
(C)$[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$(III)$0.8\,\Delta_t$
(D)$[\text{CoI}_4]^{2-}$(IV)$1.2\,\Delta_t$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
For tetrahedral complexes, the d-orbitals split into a lower energy $e$ set and a higher energy $t_2$ set. The Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) is calculated as:

$\text{CFSE} = (-0.6 n_e + 0.4 n_{t_2}) \Delta_t$

where $n_e$ and $n_{t_2}$ are the number of electrons in the $e$ and $t_2$ orbitals, respectively. Tetrahedral complexes are generally high-spin complexes.

(A) $[\text{ZnCl}_4]^{2-}$: $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ has a $3d^{10}$ configuration.
Electronic arrangement: $e^4 t_2^6$
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.6 \times 4 + 0.4 \times 6) \Delta_t = 0.0 \Delta_t$
Magnitude = $0.0 \Delta_t$ $\rightarrow$ (I)

(B) $[\text{CuCl}_4]^{2-}$: $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ has a $3d^9$ configuration.
Electronic arrangement: $e^4 t_2^5$
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.6 \times 4 + 0.4 \times 5) \Delta_t = -0.4 \Delta_t$
Magnitude = $0.4 \Delta_t$ $\rightarrow$ (II)

(C) $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$: $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ has a $3d^8$ configuration.
Electronic arrangement: $e^4 t_2^4$
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.6 \times 4 + 0.4 \times 4) \Delta_t = -0.8 \Delta_t$
Magnitude = $0.8 \Delta_t$ $\rightarrow$ (III)

(D) $[\text{CoI}_4]^{2-}$: $\text{Co}^{2+}$ has a $3d^7$ configuration.
Electronic arrangement: $e^4 t_2^3$
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.6 \times 4 + 0.4 \times 3) \Delta_t = -1.2 \Delta_t$
Magnitude = $1.2 \Delta_t$ $\rightarrow$ (IV)

The correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

questions.question:
The ratio of the magnitudes of the crystal field stabilization energies (CFSE) of the tetrahedral complexes $[\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-}$ and $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ (expressed in units of their respective $\Delta_t$) is:
(Given: atomic numbers $\text{Co} = 27, \text{Ni} = 28$)
questions.solution:
In $[\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-}$, the oxidation state of Co is $+2$. The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{2+}$ is $3d^7$.

In a tetrahedral field, the $d$-orbitals split into a lower energy $e$ set and a higher energy $t_2$ set. Since tetrahedral complexes are generally high-spin, the electrons are filled as $e^4 t_2^3$.

The crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) is given by:

$\text{CFSE} = (-0.6 n_e + 0.4 n_{t_2}) \Delta_t$

For $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ($d^7$):

$\text{CFSE} = (-0.6 \times 4 + 0.4 \times 3) \Delta_t = -1.2 \Delta_t$

The magnitude of CFSE for $[\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-}$ is $1.2 \Delta_t$.

In $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, the oxidation state of Ni is $+2$. The electronic configuration of $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ is $3d^8$.

The electrons in the tetrahedral field are filled as $e^4 t_2^4$.

For $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($d^8$):

$\text{CFSE} = (-0.6 \times 4 + 0.4 \times 4) \Delta_t = -0.8 \Delta_t$

The magnitude of CFSE for $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ is $0.8 \Delta_t$.

The ratio of the magnitudes of their CFSE is:

$\dfrac{1.2}{0.8} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Answer: $3 : 2$

questions.q: For a $d^6$ metal ion in an octahedral field, if the crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_\text{o}$) is less than the pairing energy ($P$), the correct electronic configuration is:
questions.question: For a $d^6$ metal ion in an octahedral field, if the crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_\text{o}$) is less than the pairing energy ($P$), the correct electronic configuration is:
questions.solution:
For an octahedral complex, the d-orbitals split into two sets: $t_{2g}$ (lower energy) and $e_g$ (higher energy).

Given $\Delta_\text{o} < P$, the crystal field splitting energy is less than the pairing energy. This indicates a weak field ligand, which forms a high-spin complex.

Electrons will fill the orbitals according to Hund's rule, occupying the higher energy $e_g$ orbitals singly before pairing occurs in the $t_{2g}$ orbitals.

For a $d^6$ metal ion, the first three electrons occupy the $t_{2g}$ orbitals singly ($t_{2g}^3$).

The fourth and fifth electrons occupy the $e_g$ orbitals singly ($e_g^2$).

The sixth electron pairs up in one of the $t_{2g}$ orbitals, resulting in $t_{2g}^4$.

Thus, the correct electronic configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.

Answer: $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$

This increased effective nuclear charge pulls the ligands closer to the metal ion, leading to greater repulsion with the d-electrons and resulting in a stronger crystal field splitting, not a weaker one.

Therefore, Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

The spin-only magnetic moment is given by $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given $\mu = 1.73 \text{ BM}$, we have $\sqrt{n(n+2)} = 1.73 \approx \sqrt{3}$, which gives $n = 1$.

The central metal atom is Fe (atomic number 26) with electronic configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6 4s^2$.

The ligand $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, which causes pairing of electrons in the $d$-orbitals.

For Fe in $+3$ oxidation state, the electronic configuration is $3d^5$. In the presence of a strong field ligand, the configuration becomes $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$, which has exactly $1$ unpaired electron.

For Fe in $+2$ oxidation state, the electronic configuration is $3d^6$. In the presence of a strong field ligand, the configuration becomes $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$, which has $0$ unpaired electrons.

Thus, the oxidation state of Fe is $+3$.

The charge on the complex ion $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$ is $+3 + 6(-1) = -3$.

To balance the $-3$ charge, $3$ $\text{K}^+$ ions are required. Therefore, the formula of the compound is $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$.

Comparing this with $\text{K}_x[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$, we get $x = 3$.

An octahedral complex of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ with a monodentate ligand $L$ exhibits a spin-only magnetic moment of $1.73\text{ BM}$. The number of unpaired electrons in the $e_g$ orbitals of the central metal is ____.
(Given: atomic number of Fe = 26)
questions.question:
An octahedral complex of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ with a monodentate ligand $L$ exhibits a spin-only magnetic moment of $1.73\text{ BM}$. The number of unpaired electrons in the $e_g$ orbitals of the central metal is ____.
(Given: atomic number of Fe = 26)
questions.solution:
The atomic number of Fe is 26, so the electronic configuration of Fe is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6 4s^2$.

For $\text{Fe}^{3+}$, the electronic configuration is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5$.

The spin-only magnetic moment is given by $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given $\mu = 1.73 \text{ BM} \approx \sqrt{3} \text{ BM}$, we get $n = 1$.

In an octahedral field, the $3d$ orbitals split into $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ sets. For a $d^5$ system to have exactly 1 unpaired electron, the ligand must be a strong field ligand, resulting in a low-spin complex.

The electrons will pair up in the lower energy $t_{2g}$ orbitals, giving the crystal field configuration $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$.

Since there are no electrons in the $e_g$ orbitals, the number of unpaired electrons in the $e_g$ orbitals is 0.

Answer: $0$

questions.q: The complex ion $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$ is diamagnetic in nature. The number of $d$-orbitals of nickel involved in its hybridisation is ____.
questions.question: The complex ion $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$ is diamagnetic in nature. The number of $d$-orbitals of nickel involved in its hybridisation is ____.
questions.solution:
The oxidation state of Ni in $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$ is $+2$.

The electronic configuration of Ni is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8 4s^2$.

The electronic configuration of Ni$^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8$.

Since CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand and the complex is diamagnetic, all unpaired $3d$ electrons are paired up. This leaves one $3d$ orbital empty.

To accommodate four pairs of electrons from four CN$^-$ ligands, the metal ion undergoes $dsp^2$ hybridization.

The orbitals involved in $dsp^2$ hybridization are one $3d$, one $4s$, and two $4p$ orbitals.

Therefore, the number of $d$-orbitals involved in the hybridization is $1$.

Answer: $1$

questions.q: The complex ions $[\text{PdCl}_4]^{2-}$ and $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ are diamagnetic and paramagnetic respectively. The geometries of $[\text{PdCl}_4]^{2-}$ and $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ are respectively:
questions.question: The complex ions $[\text{PdCl}_4]^{2-}$ and $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ are diamagnetic and paramagnetic respectively. The geometries of $[\text{PdCl}_4]^{2-}$ and $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
In $[\text{PdCl}_4]^{2-}$, Pd is in the $+2$ oxidation state with a $4d^8$ electronic configuration. Since Pd belongs to the 4d transition series, the crystal field splitting energy is large. Thus, even with a weak field ligand like $\text{Cl}^-$, pairing of electrons occurs, resulting in $dsp^2$ hybridization. The complex is diamagnetic and has a square planar geometry.

In $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, Ni is in the $+2$ oxidation state with a $3d^8$ electronic configuration. Since $\text{Cl}^-$ is a weak field ligand, it does not cause pairing of the 3d electrons. The hybridization is $sp^3$, resulting in a tetrahedral geometry with two unpaired electrons, making it paramagnetic.

Thus, the geometries are square planar and tetrahedral respectively.

Answer: square planar and tetrahedral

questions.question: The difference in the spin-only magnetic moment values of the complexes $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ and $[\text{Co(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ is ______ BM. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:

The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7$.

Since $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is a weak field ligand, pairing of electrons does not take place prior to filling of $e_g$ orbitals. The configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^2$.

Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 3$.

Spin-only magnetic moment, $\mu_1 = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87 \text{ BM}$.

In $[\text{Co(CN)}_6]^{3-}$, the oxidation state of Co is $+3$.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$.

Since $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of electrons. The configuration is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$.

Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 0$.

Spin-only magnetic moment, $\mu_2 = 0 \text{ BM}$.

Difference in magnetic moments $= 3.87 - 0 = 3.87 \text{ BM}$.

The nearest integer is $4$.

Answer: $4$

Consider the following coordination complexes:
$[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$, $[\text{Cr}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$, $[\text{Cr}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$, $[\text{CrF}_6]^{3-}$

The number of complexes among the above that absorb light of a longer wavelength than $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is ____.
questions.question:
Consider the following coordination complexes:
$[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$, $[\text{Cr}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$, $[\text{Cr}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$, $[\text{CrF}_6]^{3-}$

The number of complexes among the above that absorb light of a longer wavelength than $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is ____.
questions.solution:
The energy of the absorbed light corresponds to the crystal field splitting energy $\Delta_o$.

$E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} \Rightarrow \lambda \propto \dfrac{1}{\Delta_o}$

For a complex to absorb light of a longer wavelength than $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$, its crystal field splitting energy $\Delta_o$ must be smaller. This occurs when the ligands are weaker field ligands than $\text{NH}_3$.

According to the spectrochemical series, the order of ligand field strength is:

$\text{F}^- < \text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{NH}_3 < \text{en} < \text{CN}^-$

The ligands weaker than $\text{NH}_3$ are $\text{F}^-$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Therefore, the complexes $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ and $[\text{CrF}_6]^{3-}$ have a smaller $\Delta_o$ and will absorb light of a longer wavelength than $[\text{Cr}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$.

The number of such complexes is $2$.

Answer: $2$

Among the octahedral coordination entities $[\text{Mn(C}_2\text{O}_4\text{)}_3]^{3-}$, $[\text{Mn(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ and $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$, consider the complex that absorbs light of the shortest wavelength.
Let $x$ be the oxidation state of the central metal ion and $y$ be the number of unpaired electrons in that complex.
The value of $(x + y)$ is ____.
(Given: atomic number of Mn = 25)
questions.question:
Among the octahedral coordination entities $[\text{Mn(C}_2\text{O}_4\text{)}_3]^{3-}$, $[\text{Mn(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ and $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$, consider the complex that absorbs light of the shortest wavelength.
Let $x$ be the oxidation state of the central metal ion and $y$ be the number of unpaired electrons in that complex.
The value of $(x + y)$ is ____.
(Given: atomic number of Mn = 25)
questions.solution:
The oxidation state of the central metal ion Mn in all three complexes can be calculated as follows:
For $[\text{Mn(C}_2\text{O}_4\text{)}_3]^{3-}$: $x + 3(-2) = -3 \Rightarrow x = +3$
For $[\text{Mn(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$: $x + 6(0) = +3 \Rightarrow x = +3$
For $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$: $x + 6(-1) = -3 \Rightarrow x = +3$
Thus, the oxidation state of Mn in all complexes is $+3$, so $x = 3$.

The energy of the absorbed light is directly proportional to the crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_o$), and inversely proportional to the wavelength ($\lambda = \dfrac{hc}{\Delta_o}$). Therefore, the complex that absorbs light of the shortest wavelength must have the largest $\Delta_o$.

According to the spectrochemical series, the strength of the given ligands follows the order:
$\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} < \text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{CN}^-$

Since $\text{CN}^-$ is the strongest field ligand, $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ has the maximum crystal field splitting energy and absorbs light of the shortest wavelength.

Now, we find the number of unpaired electrons ($y$) in $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$.
The atomic number of Mn is 25, so its electronic configuration is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$.
For $\text{Mn}^{3+}$, the electronic configuration is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4$.
Because $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, the crystal field splitting energy is greater than the pairing energy ($\Delta_o > P$). This results in a low-spin complex where electrons pair up in the lower energy $t_{2g}$ orbitals before occupying the $e_g$ orbitals.
The $d^4$ configuration in an octahedral strong field is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^0$.
Distributing 4 electrons in the three $t_{2g}$ orbitals gives one paired set and two unpaired electrons ($\uparrow\downarrow, \uparrow, \uparrow$).
Thus, the number of unpaired electrons is $y = 2$.

Finally, the value of $(x + y)$ is:
$x + y = 3 + 2 = 5$

Answer: $5$

A coordination complex absorbs light at an absorption maximum of $497 \text{ nm}$. The crystal field splitting energy of the complex in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer) is ____.
(Given: $hc = 1.988 \times 10^{-25} \text{ J m}$, $N_A = 6.02 \times 10^{23} \text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
A coordination complex absorbs light at an absorption maximum of $497 \text{ nm}$. The crystal field splitting energy of the complex in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer) is ____.
(Given: $hc = 1.988 \times 10^{-25} \text{ J m}$, $N_A = 6.02 \times 10^{23} \text{ mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The energy of one photon is given by the Planck-Einstein relation:

$E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$

The crystal field splitting energy for one mole of the complex is:

$E_{\text{mol}} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} \times N_A$

Substituting the given values:

$E_{\text{mol}} = \dfrac{1.988 \times 10^{-25} \text{ J m}}{497 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}} \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} \text{ mol}^{-1}$

$E_{\text{mol}} = \left( 4 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J} \right) \times \left( 6.02 \times 10^{23} \text{ mol}^{-1} \right)$

$E_{\text{mol}} = 24.08 \times 10^4 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

$E_{\text{mol}} = 240.8 \times 10^3 \text{ J mol}^{-1} = 240.8 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, the crystal field splitting energy is $241 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $241$

questions.question: The complex $[\text{Ti(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ absorbs light at a wavelength of $498\text{ nm}$, which corresponds to the blue-green region of the visible spectrum. The observed colour of this complex is:
questions.solution:
The observed colour of a coordination complex is the complementary colour of the wavelength of light it absorbs.

The complex $[\text{Ti(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ contains $\text{Ti}^{3+}$ which has a $3d^1$ electronic configuration. In its octahedral field, the single $d$-electron occupies the $t_{2g}$ level.

When white light falls on the complex, it absorbs light in the blue-green region (at $498\text{ nm}$) to excite the electron from the $t_{2g}$ level to the $e_g$ level ($t_{2g}^1 e_g^0 \rightarrow t_{2g}^0 e_g^1$).

The complementary colour of blue-green is violet. Therefore, the transmitted light is violet, making the complex appear violet in colour.

Answer: Violet

The presence of one unpaired electron in the $d$-orbital allows for a $d-d$ transition (from $t_{2g}$ to $e_g$). The absorption of light in the visible region results in the violet colour of the complex.

Thus, the colours are due to ligand-to-metal charge transfer and $d-d$ transition, respectively.

Statement (D) is incorrect. The chelate effect is primarily driven by a large positive entropy change ($\Delta S^\circ$), not by enthalpy change ($\Delta H^\circ$).

Therefore, only statements (A) and (C) are correct.

The primary thermodynamic factor responsible for this enhanced stability is:
questions.question: When water molecules in $[\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$ are replaced by ethane-1,2-diamine (en) or ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$), the resulting complex $[\text{Ni(en)}_3]^{2+}$ is thermodynamically much more stable than $[\text{Ni(NH}_3)_6]^{2+}$. The primary thermodynamic factor responsible for this enhanced stability is:
options: The significantly higher crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) of ethane-1,2-diamine, making its coordination highly exothermic.
A large positive standard entropy change ($\Delta S^\circ$) accompanying the formation of $[\text{Ni(en)}_3]^{2+}$ due to a net increase in the number of free particles.
A large negative standard entropy change ($\Delta S^\circ$) due to the formation of a highly ordered and rigid chelate ring structure.
A large negative standard enthalpy change ($\Delta H^\circ$) because bidentate ligands form intrinsically stronger coordinate bonds than monodentate ligands.
questions.solution:
The substitution of water molecules by ammonia and ethane-1,2-diamine can be represented by the following equilibria:

$[\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+} + 6\text{NH}_3 \rightleftharpoons [\text{Ni(NH}_3)_6]^{2+} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$

$[\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+} + 3\text{en} \rightleftharpoons [\text{Ni(en)}_3]^{2+} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$

In the first reaction, $7$ particles react to form $7$ particles, resulting in a very small entropy change. In the second reaction, $4$ particles react to form $7$ particles, leading to a net increase in the number of free particles in the system. This causes a large positive standard entropy change ($\Delta S^\circ$).

Since $\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ$, a large positive $\Delta S^\circ$ makes $\Delta G^\circ$ significantly more negative, which corresponds to a much higher thermodynamic stability for the chelate complex $[\text{Ni(en)}_3]^{2+}$. This entropy-driven stabilization is known as the chelate effect.

Answer: A large positive standard entropy change ($\Delta S^\circ$) accompanying the formation of $[\text{Ni(en)}_3]^{2+}$ due to a net increase in the number of free particles.

questions.solution:
The complex ion $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ has $6$ water molecules acting as monodentate ligands in its coordination sphere.

$\text{EDTA}^{4-}$ (ethylenediaminetetraacetate) is a hexadentate ligand, which means it can form $6$ coordinate bonds with the central metal ion simultaneously.

When one $\text{EDTA}^{4-}$ ion coordinates with the $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ion, it replaces all the water molecules to satisfy the coordination number of $6$ for iron.

The reaction is given by:
$[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+} + \text{EDTA}^{4-} \rightarrow [\text{Fe}(\text{EDTA})]^{-} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Thus, $6$ water molecules are displaced.

Answer: $6$

questions.question: In the qualitative analysis of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions, the addition of potassium hexacyanoferrate(II) solution yields an intense Prussian blue precipitate. The value of $2x + y + z$ is ____.
questions.solution:
The reaction of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions with potassium hexacyanoferrate(II), $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$, produces an intense Prussian blue precipitate.

The chemical equation for the formation of Prussian blue is:
$4\text{Fe}^{3+} + 3[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-} \rightarrow \text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]_3$

In the formula of Prussian blue, $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]_3$:
The iron ion present outside the coordination sphere is $\text{Fe}^{3+}$, so its oxidation state is $x = 3$.
The iron ion present inside the coordination sphere is $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, so its oxidation state is $y = 2$.
The coordination number of the iron ion inside the coordination sphere (number of cyanide ligands attached) is $z = 6$.

We need to find the value of $2x + y + z$:
$2x + y + z = 2(3) + 2 + 6 = 6 + 2 + 6 = 14$

Answer: $14$

questions.question: Nessler's reagent is an alkaline solution of a mercury complex used in qualitative analysis for the detection of ammonium ions. The coordination number and the oxidation state of mercury in this complex are, respectively:
questions.solution:
Nessler's reagent is an alkaline solution of potassium tetraiodomercurate(II), whose chemical formula is $K_2[HgI_4]$.

The complex ion present in this reagent is $[HgI_4]^{2-}$.

In this complex, the central mercury atom is surrounded by four iodide ($I^-$) ligands. Therefore, the coordination number of mercury is $4$.

Let the oxidation state of mercury be $x$. The sum of the oxidation states of all atoms in the complex ion must equal its net charge:

$x + 4(-1) = -2$

$x - 4 = -2$

$x = +2$

Thus, the coordination number is $4$ and the oxidation state is $+2$.

Answer: 4 and +2

questions.question: In the extraction of gold, the metal is leached with a dilute aqueous solution of $\text{NaCN}$ in the presence of air to form a water-soluble coordination complex. The coordination number and the oxidation state of gold in this complex are, respectively:
questions.solution:
The extraction of gold involves leaching the metal with a dilute aqueous solution of $\text{NaCN}$ in the presence of air (oxygen). The balanced chemical equation for this process is:

$4\text{Au} + 8\text{NaCN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 4\text{Na}[\text{Au}(\text{CN})_2] + 4\text{NaOH}$

The water-soluble coordination complex formed is $\text{Na}[\text{Au}(\text{CN})_2]$, which contains the complex ion $[\text{Au}(\text{CN})_2]^-$.

In this complex ion, the gold atom is bonded to two cyanide ($\text{CN}^-$) ligands. Therefore, the coordination number of gold is $2$.

Let the oxidation state of gold be $x$. Since each cyanide ligand carries a charge of $-1$ and the overall charge on the complex ion is $-1$, we have:

$x + 2(-1) = -1$

$x - 2 = -1$

$x = +1$

The oxidation state of gold in the complex is $+1$.

Answer: 2 and +1

Square planar complexes possess a molecular plane of symmetry (the plane containing the metal ion and all four ligands). Due to the presence of this plane of symmetry, cisplatin is achiral and does not exhibit optical isomerism.

Since both chloride ions are present inside the coordination sphere, they are non-ionizable. Thus, cisplatin does not yield a precipitate of $\text{AgCl}$ upon treatment with aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$.

It is a neutral complex containing two ammine and two chlorido ligands.

Therefore, the statement claiming that it exhibits optical isomerism is incorrect.

The square planar complex $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{ClBr}]$ is of the type $\text{Ma}_2\text{bc}$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism, existing as cis and trans isomers. Since square planar complexes possess a molecular plane of symmetry, they do not show optical isomerism. Thus, the total number of stereoisomers is $x = 2$.

The trans isomer has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive. The cis isomer lacks a plane of symmetry and is optically active, existing as a pair of enantiomers (d and l forms). Thus, the total number of stereoisomers is $y = 1 + 2 = 3$.

The value of $x + y = 2 + 3 = 5$.

Answer: $5$
